Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Money, work & business · Work & responsibility · Civic life: news, government & the law

negotiate verb

also negotiate terms, negotiate a deal, negotiate peace, negotiating, hold talks, strike a deal, bargain

classical

Caes. BG 1.13.3: Is ita cum Caesare ēgit
Traupman 187: agere cum aliquō dē pāce, to have peace negotiations with someone

agō cum aliquō dē aliquā rē

verb phrase: agō, agere, ēgī, āctum

treat with someone about something, negotiate

The plain classical way to say it (Lewis & Short s.v. agō): to negotiate peace, dē pāce agere; to put forward terms, condiciōnēs ferre (see propose). The talks themselves are colloquium (see negotiation).

Other words

  • pacīscor, pacīscī, pactus sum — bargain, settle terms, make a deal

    also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 3.12.1: sed jam nunc pacīscor

    To bargain and come to terms (with long ī, de Vaan 452; see haggle, agreement); the deal made is pactum.

  • trānsigō, trānsigere, trānsēgī, trānsāctum — settle, conclude (a deal)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 13.14.2: negōtium (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. negotiate, after Milton (1674)

    Classically to carry business through to the end, to settle it: what one does once the negotiating is over; cum aliquō trānsigere, to come to a settlement with someone (Lewis & Short). M-O gives it for negotiating itself. Its other sense is to run through with a weapon (poetry and later prose).

Examples

  • Is ita cum Caesare ēgit: sī pācem populus Rōmānus cum Helvētiīs faceret, in eam partem itūrōs atque ibi futūrōs Helvētiōs ubi eōs Caesar cōnstituisset atque esse voluisset

    He negotiated with Caesar as follows: if the Roman people made peace with the Helvetii, they would go and stay wherever Caesar settled them and wished them to beCaes. BG 1.13.3

  • veniam ad cēnam, sed jam nunc pacīscor, sit expedīta sit parca

    I’ll come to dinner, but I’m setting my terms now: let it be quick, let it be frugalPlin. Ep. 3.12.1

See also negotiation, haggle, agreement, propose, contract.

SourcesLewis & Short: ago · Lewis & Short: paciscor · Lewis & Short: transigo
